answer: A gale of cheap fake identities breaks against a time-locked bond: each agent locks a deposit that only a quartz-hard record of verified, useful work can release, so every alias costs real capital held hostage. Reputation then grows like a vine, branching only through attested exchanges with established agents, and one failed audit prunes the whole branch and burns the bond. Forging a thousand voices means funding a thousand deposits and losing each on detection, while an honest agent pays once.
